div.head: III Em 1
div.ab: [I.] Imprimis ut omnes iurent in nomine Domini, pro quo sanctum illud sanctum est, fidelitatem Eadmundo regi, sicut homo debet esse fidelis domino suo, sine omni controuersia et seductione, in manifesto, in occulto, et in amando quod amabit, nolendo quod nolet; et a die qua iuramentum hoc dabitur, ut nemo concelet hoc in fratre uel proximo suo plus quam in extraneo.

Imprimis, ut omnes jurent in nomine Domini, pro quo sanctum illud sanctum est, fidelitatem Eadmundo regi, sicut homo debet esse fidelis domino suo, sine omni controversia et seductione, in manifesto, in occulto, et in amando quod amabit, nolendo quod nolet; et a die qua juramentum hoc dabitur, ut nemo concelet hoc in fratre vel proximo suo plus quam in extraneo.

In the first place, all shall swear in the name of the Lord, before whom that holy thing is holy, that they will be faithful to King Edmund, even as it behoves a man to be faithful to his lord, without any dispute or dissension, openly or in secret, favouring what he favours and discountenancing what he discountenances. And from the day on which this oath shall be rendered, let no-one conceal the breach of it in a brother or a relation of his, any more than in a stranger.

Vgl. Gl Königstreue 7.—(An?)ærest þæt ealle [nicht etwa bloss wie bei II Ew 1, 1 die Witan] swerien on Dryhtenes naman, þe þes haligdom is fore halig, hylde las Or. laut II Ew 1, 1, Swer 1 und I Cn 20, 1.—Über die Bed. von sanctum s. Gl Heiligtum 1; Eidesform 7 ff. Zunächst ist an Reliquie zu denken. Nur diese verstehen Thorpe, Toller 305b Z. 1

Cf. Gl Königstreue 7.—(An?)ærest þæt ealle [not, say, merely the Witan, as in II Ew 1, 1] swerien on Dryhtenes naman, þe þes haligdom is fore halig, hylde was the reading of the original, according to II Ew 1, 1, Swer 1 and I Cn 20, 1.—On the meaning of sanctum see Gl Heiligtum 1; Eidesform 7 ff. The first thing to think of is a relic. Thorpe and Toller 305b l. 1 understand only this

Dieser Untertaneneid—denn alle sollen ihn leisten—baut sich auf dem Mannschafteide (s. d. Gl 2e) auf. Er geht wie im Umfang der Schwörenden so im Inhalt des Geschworenen über Eadwards Forderung hinaus. Offenbar soll Königstreue (s. d. Gl 7b) über Vassallität gehen; so Pol Mai I 67. Die Formel kann Fränkisch beeinflusst sein. Die Nachahmung des Gefolgseides durch den Untertaneneid liegt auch in der Fränkischen Monarchie vor; Brunner Zs. Savigny RG 1914, 457

This oath of subjects—for all are to take it—is built upon the oath of homage (see that word in Gl 2e). It goes beyond Eadward’s demand both in the range of those who swear and in the content of what is sworn. Evidently loyalty to the king (see that word in Gl 7b) is meant to take precedence over vassalage; so Pol Mai I 67. The formula may be under Frankish influence. The imitation of the oath of the retinue by the oath of subjects is also found in the Frankish monarchy; Brunner Zs. Savigny RG 1914, 457
hold his hlaforde, butan brægde ⁊ biswice las Or.
hold his hlaforde, butan brægde ⁊ biswice was the reading of the original.
seductio und seditio stehen im juristischen Anglolatein des MA. synonym für ‘Verrat’; Pol Mai II 500
seductio and seditio are used synonymously for ‘treason’ in the juristic Anglo-Latin of the Middle Ages; Pol Mai II 500
lufian þæt he lufað, ascunian þæt he ascunað las Or. laut II Ew 1, 1 und Swer 1
lufian þæt he lufað, ascunian þæt he ascunað was the reading of the original, according to II Ew 1, 1 and Swer 1

hoc muss die Verletzung einer Bürgerpflicht bedeuten, entweder des Ehrlichkeitsversprechens (s. d. Gl 1—4), das von Eadmunds beiden Vorgängern allgemein eingeführt war, oder dieser Königstreue.—Nichts zu verhehlen beteuert der Eid auch der Rügegeschworenen; s. d. Gl 1. Für extraneus hatte Or. fremde laut III Eg 7, 2

hoc must mean the breach of a civic duty, either of the promise of honesty (see that word in Gl 1—4), which had been introduced generally by Eadmund’s two predecessors, or of this loyalty to the king.—The oath of the jurors of presentment also affirms that nothing will be concealed; see that word in Gl 1. For extraneus the original had fremde, according to III Eg 7, 2

Cf. the A.S. phrase þe ðes haligdom is fore halig, Oath Formulae, 1; 2. Liebermann suggests that the reference here is probably to a relic of some sort. Oaths were also rendered on the altar (cf. Hl. 16, 2; Wi. 18–21), on the Cross etc. (see Liebermann, ii, Eidesform, 7 ff.).
Liebermann understands this to mean an oath sworn by all the king’s subjects, presumably all those who were qualified to take part in the assemblies of the hundred and the county.

Liebermann suggests that the original A.S. text read butan brægde ⁊ biswice, cf. I Edw. 1, 5, where, however, the Latin rendering of butan brægde is sine figmento. The word controversia means literally ‘dispute.’ The words seductio and seditio are regularly used in juristic Anglo-Latin of the Middle Ages meaning ‘treason’ (see Pollock and Maitland, Hist. of Eng. Law, ii. p. 502).
It is not clear whether these adverbial phrases qualify the preceding words or are to be taken as parallel to them and like them dependent on fidelis.
Cf. II Edw. Pre. § 1.
This interpretation follows Liebermann’s emendation to a die qua which certainly gives a better sense.
